## Real browser E2E and uncached performance proof

Application source: `af2cd07b25d90a7318a4746714e79fc945f3e38c`. The screenshots are **before/after enabling search in the same candidate**, not a simulated pre-patch UI. Chromium renders the actual built Control UI served by a normal isolated Gateway. The candidate was installed from a normal npm-packed tarball with ordinary install safety/capability checks; no Gateway RPC or provider HTTP responses are mocked.

### Before

DeepSeek is present in Search settings and provider setup, with search disabled and credentials inherited from the protected environment.

![Before enabling DeepSeek search](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/62072263-4d25-45b6-b7a9-8a4d6af32b88)

### After

Browser controls save the provider/enabled settings; normal Gateway activation publishes them. The UI then completes a real authenticated `webSearch.test`, displays sources, and retains the selection after reload. An independent CLI read confirms persistence. Served entry-JS SHA256 matches the built UI. No model inference was requested, and no credential value appears in the captures.

![After enabling DeepSeek and completing a real search](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e09b86ca-7b84-4383-ae50-81c72a9cbc2a)

E2E: **1/1 passes**, 9.93 seconds test body / 55.71 seconds wrapper wall including fixture/compiler preparation. Explicit opt-in is required; the default path skips paid work and does not import the live Gateway/browser fixture graph (verified skipped run: 3.54 seconds wrapper wall). Earlier failed attempts were harness issues—compiler preparation, a development-directory symlink rejected by the install scanner, incorrect route/control selectors, and minimal-fixture activation—not passing product proof. The final run uses the packed candidate and normal Gateway activation, with safety checks intact.

### Uncached benchmark

Node v26.8.2, Linux x64, AMD EPYC 9555. Live requests are sequential, `count: 3`, `need_content: false`, **`cacheTtlMinutes: 0`**, matching endpoint/auth/guard/proxy and alternating pair order. Exactly 12 successful live requests: six provider calls and six transport baselines.

| Path | Samples | Median | Observed p95 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Compiled DeepSeek provider, real API, uncached | 6 | 536.54 ms | 685.37 ms |
| Same guarded HTTP + JSON baseline, real API | 6 | 499.56 ms | 566.72 ms |
| Real full `web_search`, explicit, warm HTTP fixture | 90 | 3.056 ms | 5.793 ms |
| Real full `web_search`, automatic, warm HTTP fixture | 90 | 3.011 ms | 5.887 ms |
| Direct provider with the same fixture/harness | 90 | 0.371 ms | 0.508 ms |
| Actual five-row output normalization | 3,000 | 0.0495 ms/call | — |

At six samples, observed p95 is just the maximum, not a population-tail estimate. The median paired provider-minus-baseline difference is **−0.45 ms**; network variation and initialization prevent interpreting the independent median difference as provider overhead. Source/TSX cold import/first-execution measurements are **not deployed compiled-Gateway startup claims**.

The API/network path dominates live latency. No new production caches were added, and no 100× speedup is claimed. Profiling identifies existing repeated unrelated activation/readiness work (channel/catalog/setup checks) as the main local follow-up; the correct direction is removing redundant preparation through the existing owner, not more caches or bypassing plugin authority. The ~3 ms warm tool path does not justify a speculative core rewrite in this provider PR. Other small observed work includes repeated WSL detection, result copying/URL processing, and cache-key preparation at TTL zero; these are not measured live bottlenecks.

All live benchmark rows returned three results without a local cache hit. Compiled artifact hashes, per-request timings, resource measurements, source hashes, and CPU profiles were retained for inspection. The benchmark source is `af2cd07b25d90a7318a4746714e79fc945f3e38c`; the pre-publication build-info label is `8e236614…`, so artifact hashes—not that version label—identify execution.

nodes.body:
Thanks for landing #175729 (and the credential follow-up #178544).

**Request:** please consider shipping DeepSeek web search on the **extended-stable** line (next 2026.9.x maintenance release). extended-stable users currently have no way to use it — the documented flow (install the official DeepSeek plugin, select `deepseek` as the `web_search` provider) is unreachable there.

What I can observe from the published artifacts (not only one install):

- `@openclaw/deepseek-provider@2026.9.34`: `tools: []`, capabilities only `text-inference`, and no search code anywhere in the package.
- `@openclaw/deepseek-provider@2026.10.7` and `@2026.10.10-beta.3` (official npm tarball, ~43 KB): `dist/` contains only `api`, `index`, `models`, `onboard`, `provider-catalog`, `provider-discovery`, `provider-policy-api`, `stream`, `thinking`. There is no `web-search-provider.runtime` file, and the string `tools/search` does not appear anywhere in the tarball.

So the feature appears to be on `main` but absent from the published plugin packages we can install. Could you confirm:

1. which release is expected to ship the search runtime, and
2. whether an extended-stable backport is feasible (even without Fetch, i.e. search-only as scoped in the PR)?

Happy to run a build against `POST https://api.deepseek.com/v1/tools/search` and report results if that helps.

Follow-up 12 days after merge — the gap is now consistent across **every** published line, so I think this needs an explicit answer rather than more waiting.

**Source state**
- `extensions/deepseek/web-search-provider.ts` exists on `main` and is actively maintained there (follow-up commits, e.g. `f1036c36` on 2026-10-26).
- The same path returns **404** on every release tag I checked: `v2026.9.36`, `v2026.10.9`, `v2026.10.10-beta.5`.
- No revert PR found for #175729.

**Published artifacts**
- `@openclaw/deepseek-provider@2026.10.9` and `@2026.10.10-beta.5` (official registry tarballs, ~44 KB each) still ship only `api / index / models / onboard / provider-catalog / provider-discovery / provider-policy-api / stream / thinking`. No search runtime file, and the string `tools/search` does not appear anywhere in either tarball.

**Practical impact**
`web_search` still cannot select `deepseek` on extended-stable (2026.9.36), stable (2026.10.9), or beta (2026.10.10-beta.5).

**Questions**
1. Is DeepSeek search intentionally held back from release branches, or is the merge missing from the release lineage?
2. What is the ETA for a build that actually ships it?
3. If it will only land on the 10.x line, is an extended-stable backport out of scope?

Happy to run a build against `POST https://api.deepseek.com/v1/tools/search` and report results if that helps move it forward.
